reproduce.title: Disable Key Or Shortcut does not disable the first key of the combo for the specified app
prerequisites: Use the exact screenshot mapping and exefile.exe target.
Use a normal key-event test application for comparison; preserve other mappings unchanged.
reproduce.expected_result: The completed configured shortcut is blocked where supported; unrelated modifier use remains usable.
steps: Press the modifier alone and record whether ordinary modifier behavior remains available.
Press the complete disabled shortcut and record the game action, not merely the modifier indicator.
Compare the same mapping in a normal hook-based test target; maintainer-side checks distinguish raw-input events from unsuppressed hook events.

known_information: The report names EVE exefile.exe and supplies screenshots of an app-specific disabled shortcut.
The first key is seen by the application while the completed shortcut second key is blocked; the reporter says this is not limited to modifier pairs.
The supplied images show Unknown key and an ALT- prefix; the text example mentions SHIFT-.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue body and public discussion, current ownership, labels and linked-work history.
Read the exact app target and both mapping screenshots described in the report.
Keyboard Manager handles app-specific shortcut matches after resolving current modifier state; game input delivery must be distinguished from low-level-hook delivery.
inferences: This may reflect completed-chord semantics or a game raw-input path rather than failure to suppress the configured completed shortcut.
issue_context.summary: Disabling a two-key app shortcut does not necessarily mean suppressing its first modifier before the chord is known.
issue_context.analysis: The old generic shortcut-suppression fix was not justified. Reproduce completed-chord behavior in a normal hook consumer and EVE before deciding whether a product change is needed; blanket prefix-modifier suppression could break unrelated shortcuts.

fix_assessment.rationale: No code change to suppress a modifier before any chord is known is justified by completed-shortcut disabling semantics; first determine whether the completed chord itself escapes suppression.

judgment.rationale: The old generic shortcut-suppression fix was not justified. Reproduce completed-chord behavior in a normal hook consumer and EVE before deciding whether a product change is needed; blanket prefix-modifier suppression could break unrelated shortcuts.
judgment.recommended_action: Establish whether the completed disabled chord still acts, and whether EVE observes raw input independently of hook suppression.
